Every rev from 1.0.3 to 1.0.14 was an OFF-NNN knob that left the golden byte-unchanged and re-blessed no baseline; this one MOVES THE GOLDEN'S PIXELS ON PURPOSE, and that is what GOLDEN REFREEZE BATCH 2 records. measureMarkupExtent step 1 used to bound every `<g transform="translate(...)">` by a plus/minus r square where r was the largest NUMBER appearing anywhere in that group's markup STRING, so an A-4 fault-current pennant reading "41,837A" claimed plus/minus 837 px around its anchor and even a digit-free one claimed plus/minus 700 off `font-weight="700"`, against true geometry of about plus/minus 100 px (FL-0007; the `< 10000` clamp in the old code was the author's own tell that the scrape was picking up non-coordinates). addin_dll.embeds_map_note: The family-map bytes the shipping DEDARMS.dll ACTUALLY embeds, byte-verified when it was blessed by extracting the .NET manifest resource (length-prefixed at its offset) and hashing it. sync_gate's surviving lockstep check asserts that THIS FIELD equals family_map.sha256 — i.e. the DLL that ships is in step with the map this repo publishes — waived to a KNOWN-STALE warning only while stale_pending_rebuild is true. ⚠️ PHASE 7b CHANGED WHAT ELSE ASSERTS THIS. Until 2026-07-31 a sibling check ALSO re-extracted the real embed from a DLL on disk and compared it to this field (the 'honesty' check), so the field could not lie about an artifact this repo held. That DLL has left, that check went with it, and the toolkit's T4 now performs the re-extraction against ITS OWN pin. CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: on this side the field is now MAINTAINED BY HAND. Re-bless it here in the same change-set as any toolkit rebuild that moves the embed — nothing in this repo can catch you forgetting.
addin_dll.stale_pending_rebuild_note: LEFT FALSE 2026-07-30 by Phase 5c, deliberately, after briefly setting it true and being corrected by sync_gate. This flag has a NARROW meaning — 'the DLL embed is knowingly out of step with the current family map' — and it WAIVES the map<->DLL lockstep assertion to a warning. It is NOT a general honesty flag. ⚠️ THE HONESTY FLAG IT USED TO SIT BESIDE (runtime_unverified) IS NO LONGER IN THIS FILE — it moved to the toolkit manifest with the artifact on 2026-07-31, and all three assemblies are still marked unverified there. Setting THIS flag to mean that one silently disables a real check. The lockstep is NOT broken today: the embed is df7cfc4f, identical to family_map.sha256, because the Phase 5a/5b restructure changed where the map file lives and what LogicalName it carries but never its BYTES.

null_byte_in_strip_compare.all_nul_bearing_files_note: ADDED 2026-07-30 (Phase 5 verification). This entry named ONE file while THREE carry NUL bytes (5 bytes total) - the runbook and FL-0013 had recorded that, this machine-truth file had not. Re-derived by byte-count differencing (tr -d), because grep -P is unavailable on this box and $'\x00' is empty in bash (it silently matches everything). ⚠️ RE-DERIVED AGAIN 2026-07-31 AFTER PHASE 7b: TWO OF THE THREE FILES LEFT THIS REPO. ReplayPreflight.cs and RibbonBuilder.cs moved to `Mayo_Claude_Workspace/DEDARMS Revit Toolkit` with the add-in; their 3 NUL bytes went with them and are that repo's business now. THIS repo holds ONE NUL-bearing file and 2 NUL bytes, re-measured by the same tr -d differencing (8826 B raw, 8824 B stripped). ⚠️ THE `grep -a` RULE IS UNCHANGED AND STILL PERMANENT, IN BOTH REPOS — one remaining NUL-bearing file is exactly as capable of silently emptying a sweep as three were. EVERY NUL IS A DELIBERATE COMPOSITE-KEY DELIMITER, not a stray: ka.join(NUL) for the JSON key-ORDER compare in G8; family+NUL+type as the Revit symbol dictionary key (self-documented in xmldoc on the very line that carries one); panelName+NUL+group for the ribbon pulldown cache. NUL is chosen precisely because it cannot occur in the strings being joined - stripping them would inject key collisions (panel AB + group empty would equal panel A + group B). FL-0013 item 4 is WILL-NOT-FIX and the grep -a rule is PERMANENT. Also corrected here: the line was recorded as 108, it is 106.
null_byte_in_strip_compare.issue: The key-comparison joins with a LITERAL NUL character (2 raw 0x00 bytes in the file), so grep/ugrep classify the file as binary and SKIP it silently. `grep -c join` returns nothing, `grep -ac join` returns 11.
null_byte_in_strip_compare.status: DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED — functionally correct and G8 passes; changing the separator risks G8. Use `grep -a` (or a binary-safe reader) when sweeping.
